children: Raw material prices have remained largely stable month-on-month in August, excluding sugar, copra and Brent crude, following a sharp increase in June. However, cumulatively for 2QFYTD27, most raw material prices remain higher quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year, which could lead to further product price hikes and pressure near-term margins in 2QFY27F, Nomura said.

"Sugar prices have risen 16% / 27% m-m / y-y amid tight near-term availability and heightened festive-season demand," Nomura said. Recent government measures, including duty-free imports and release of stocks, have started easing prices, which are 1.5% below their peak. However, the brokerage said this could pressure margins for Britannia Industries, Nestlé India, Dabur, ITC and Hindustan Unilever.

Copra prices have risen 14% m-m and 10% q-q, "negating the need for further price cuts". While anniversarisation of earlier price hikes and a recent price cut in Parachute could lower Marico's sales growth momentum, copra prices remain 33% below year-ago levels and 34% below their peak, which "should offer support to MRCO's margins and drive strong EBITDA growth".

Brent crude and HDPE prices have increased 10% and 3% m-m, respectively, and are up 26% and 42% y-y amid geopolitical uncertainties. Nomura expects this "to drive higher packaging costs across consumer companies in 2QFY27F and increase raw material costs for paint companies, despite price hikes".

Palm oil prices have stabilised m-m but remain elevated by 20% y-y in rupee terms, potentially affecting margins for Godrej Consumer Products, Hindustan Unilever, Nestlé India and Britannia. Liquid paraffin prices have softened over the past 10 days but remain 41% higher y-y, which could impact hair oil players such as Dabur and Marico and personal care companies including Hindustan Unilever and Godrej Consumer Products.

Gold prices have been volatile, rising 6% m-m but remaining 8% below their peak. "Given the recent softness from its peak, we believe gold price could drive higher volumes/footfalls for jewelry players such as Titan," Nomura said.

Tea prices have moderated 7% m-m but remain inflationary at 13% y-y, while robusta coffee prices have softened 4% m-m and 8% y-y. The latter "should continue to support NEST's and HUVR's margins", Nomura said. Maize prices rose 5% m-m for the second consecutive quarter and could add pressure to Colgate's margins.
Milk, wheat and TiO2 prices have largely remained range-bound, which should support margins for food companies such as Britannia, Nestlé and QSR players, as well as paint companies.

Nomura expects 2QFY27F margins to remain under pressure, although price hikes are likely to support sequential improvement from 3QFY27F onwards. "Consumer companies have taken price hikes in 1QFY27, which will likely optically improve sales growth but are lower than inflation; this is likely to pressure near-term (2QFY27F) margins y-y and q-q," the brokerage said.
"With the full impact of price hikes kicking in, we expect margins to sequentially improve from 3QFY27F onwards," Nomura added.

title: Britannia, Nestlé India, Godrej Consumer, paints face raw material pressure; Nomura sees 2QFY27 margin hit
